title: Sort Flow Upgrade
eyebrow: Design for approval · issues #180, #181 and #182 · nothing built yet

short.lead: This proposal covers your three Asap issues together, because all three change the same place: the Unsorted card. Sorting a task would let you rename it, write notes on it, move it to a project, find a project or label by typing, and link it to other tasks. The focus picker would then use those links to offer the task that unblocks the most work first.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes and what it needs from you. The pictures come from a clickable prototype that uses the app's own stylesheet.
items: What the Unsorted card does today

Today the card shows one item at a time. A thought gets a project, then a kind (Reminder, Build or Fix) and labels. A task gets only the kind and labels. Eight labels show before a '+50 more' pill, new labels are typed into a box separated by commas, and there is no search. Tasks have a title and a 'steps' checklist, but no notes, no subtasks and no links to other tasks. The focus picker chooses at random.

items.alt: Today's Unsorted card: title, Reminder, Build and Fix cards, eight labels and +50 more, and a New labels box
items.caption: Today's card, drawn by the app's own code with 55 labels.

items: #182: one search box for projects and labels
A 'Find a project or label…' box sits above the pickers. Typing filters the project pills and the label pills together. When nothing matches, a '+ New label' pill appears.

items.alt: Typing 're' shows Reading list under Move to project and four matching labels
items.caption: Typing “re” narrows 7 projects and 55 labels down to 1 project and 4 labels.

items: #180 and #181: edit and link while sorting

The title becomes editable and a Notes box is added. The project chip moves a task as well as a thought. A 'How does it connect?' section adds four rows: Part of, Subtasks, Waits on and Holds up. 'Part of' and 'Subtasks' search this project. 'Waits on' and 'Holds up' search every project.

items.alt: The link rows with a subtask, a waits-on task, and the Holds up search open showing a task from Portfolio site
items.caption: “Holds up” searches every project. Here it finds a task in Portfolio site.

items: The focus card shows how many tasks the current one clears the way for. When the pick has open subtasks, the card lists them and offers to start the next one. A task that is still waiting on something is skipped while anything unblocked is left.

items.alt: Two focus cards: one saying it clears the way for two tasks, one listing its subtasks with the next one highlighted
items.caption: The top card is a blocker picked first. The bottom card is a parent task pointing at its next subtask.

Subtasks and dependencies
Each task gets a parent, plus 'waits on' links to tasks in any project (#180, #181).

This adds two fields to a task. The first is its parent: one task in the same project. The second is its 'waits on' list: tasks from any project that must be done first. choices: subtasks
What should a subtask be?
A
A real task with a parent
It shows in its project, can be focused, labelled and linked, and the parent lists it.
B
Reuse the existing 'steps' checklist
This is smaller to build, but a step can't be focused, labelled or linked, so most of #180 can't work.
Issue #180 asks for subtasks that can block their parent and be suggested first. Only a real task can be suggested by the focus picker. Existing steps stay as they are.
newlabels
What happens to the 'New labels, comma-separated…' box?
A
The search box replaces it
Type a name; if no label matches, tap '+ New label'. One box instead of two.
B
Keep both boxes
Nothing you use today goes away, but the card has two text boxes that look alike.
Both boxes are for typing a label name. Merging them means one place to type, and the search shows you an existing label before you make a duplicate.
body
What does 'edit the task body' cover?
A
Title and a new Notes field
Notes is a plain-text box. Steps stay editable in the normal task editor.
B
Title, Notes and steps, all in the Unsorted card
This makes the card taller on a phone.
C
Title only
This is the smallest change, but #181 asks for more.
Tasks have no notes field today, so 'body' needs one. Steps already have a home in the task editor, and putting them here too makes the card long.
focus
How should 'suggested first' work in the focus picker?
A
Unblocked first, then whichever clears the most
A blocked task is skipped while anything else is free.
B
Tasks that have subtasks come first
This is a literal reading of the issue title, but it would point you at a parent you can't finish yet.
C
Keep it random and only show the chips
No change to the order; the links are for information only.
Issue #180 says tasks with subtasks 'name their blockers'. Read that way, the useful pick is the blocker, not the blocked parent. The card for a parent still shows up and points at its next subtask.
scope
Can 'Part of' pick a parent in another project?
A
No: same project only
The subtask lives in its parent's project. Waits on and Holds up still work across every project.
B
Yes: any project
A subtask could sit in a different project from its parent, which makes project views harder to read.
Issue #181 says 'a subtask of an existing task in that project', and says 'any project' only for dependencies.
github
Should the links sync to GitHub issues now?
A
Not yet: keep them in Focus Deck, and open a follow-up issue
They still sync between your devices, the same way your other task data does.
B
Yes: write them as GitHub sub-issues and 'blocked by' links now
This adds GitHub API work and makes the Asap fix take longer.

You asked for this as soon as possible. Every task field already syncs between your devices, so local links work everywhere you use the app. GitHub's sub-issue and dependency links are a separate job.

wrapup.summary: This proposal makes the Unsorted card search projects and labels, edit a task's title and notes, move it, and link it as a subtask or a dependency. The focus picker then uses those links.
wrapup.changing: Changed: the Unsorted card, the focus picker's order and the focus card. New: a search box, two task fields (parent and waits-on) and a Notes field. Kept: the kind cards, label ranking and steps.
wrapup.blocking: Your six answers under Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After approval, I open one parent issue with three child issues (search, editing and links, focus order), build them on the AjsAgent/sort-flow-asap branch, and send you a QA page with a pull request.
